note.headline: Megacap tech gives back the AI trade as breadth collapses to one advancer
note.standfirst: The S&P fell 4.36% and the Nasdaq 100 dropped 6.36% as Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom and Oracle were sold hard while bonds and gold caught a bid. Breadth was 1 advancer against 25 decliners, so this was not rotation, it was a single crowded trade unwinding at once.
takeaways: Semiconductor and AI-infrastructure names led the index down, with AMD off 17.26%, Tesla off 10.77%, Broadcom off 10.43% and Nvidia off 9.26%.
Breadth was the worst signal of the day: 1 advancer, 25 decliners, dispersion of 4.04.
Treasuries rallied across the curve, 10-year yield down 5bp to 4.90%, as equity selling met a safe-haven bid.
The VIX rose 69.66% to 28.18 and VIX 9-day jumped 115.01% to 32.66, pricing acute near-term stress rather than a slow grind.
note.desk_view:
This session confirms that the AI-capex trade had become a single position dressed up as a market. When Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom and Oracle all fall together by 6 to 17%, and only one name in the index closes higher, that is not sector rotation out of tech into value. It is forced or voluntary de-risking of the same crowded book. The staples complex held relatively well, Costco actually rose 1.83%, Coca-Cola was down just 0.07%, which tells you the selling was concentrated, not systemic liquidation.

The level that decides what this becomes is the 10-year yield and the VIX term structure together. Yields fell 5bp on the day even as equities were sold, a classic flight-to-quality bid that argues this is a risk-asset repricing, not a funding or liquidity event. But VIX 9-day at 32.66, well above the 3-month print of 25.55, prices a near-term shock the market expects to fade. If that inverts further, or if yields start rising alongside falling equities, the story changes from a crowded trade unwinding into something the bond market is also worried about. Watch 2s10s, down 2bp to 32bp, for any sign the curve stops cooperating with the equity narrative.
watching: Whether Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom and Oracle stabilize or see follow-through selling at the open.
VIX 9-day versus VIX 3-month, the current inversion needs to normalize for this to look like a one-day flush.
10-year yield direction, a reversal higher alongside weak equities would change the read from flight-to-quality to broader deleveraging.
Credit spreads in HYG and EMB, both softened today and are the next tell if risk aversion spreads beyond equities.
note.equities:
The S&P 500 closed down 4.36% at 7,353.73, the Nasdaq 100 fell 6.36% to 26,629.81, and the Russell 2000 dropped 4.45%, so small caps were not spared despite having no direct AI-capex exposure. The Dow's smaller loss of 3.44% reflects its lighter semiconductor weight, not any broad resilience.

Sector dispersion was stark. Technology fell 8.00%, industrials fell 4.13% and materials fell 2.91%, while consumer staples held at -0.75% and communications slipped just 0.59%. Breadth confirms the concentration: 1 advancer against 25 decliners with a dispersion reading of 4.04, the kind of print that shows up when one trade, not one macro view, is driving the tape. Costco at +1.83% and Coca-Cola flat to down 0.07% were the exceptions that prove it.
note.rates:
The curve bull-flattened modestly on a parallel shift lower, with 2s10s down 2bp to 32bp and 3m10y down 5bp to 69bp. 5s30s steepened 1bp to 59bp. The 10-year yield fell 5bp to 4.90%, the 5-year fell 5bp to 4.69%, and the 2-year fell 3bp to 4.58%, with the 30-year down 4bp to 5.28%.

Breakevens fell alongside nominal yields, the 5-year breakeven down 4bp to 2.26% and the 10-year down 2bp to 2.24%, while the 5y5y forward held at 2.22%. Real yields were little changed, the 10-year TIPS yield off 1bp to 2.64% as of the prior session's print. The MOVE index rose 4.31% to 97.92, a rates-vol move consistent with equity stress spilling into fixed income without derailing the bid for duration.
note.credit: Credit softened but did not crack. High yield (HYG) fell 0.31%, JNK fell 0.27%, and EM sovereign debt (EMB) fell 0.52%, modest moves against the scale of the equity selloff. Investment grade (LQD) actually rose 0.15%, consistent with the Treasury bid pulling IG spread product along for the ride. Leveraged loans underperformed, down 0.68%, the one pocket of credit showing real stress.
note.fx: The dollar index was little changed, up 0.08% to 101.59, masking divergent moves underneath. The yen was the standout haven flow, USD/JPY down 0.51% to 157.66, while the Swiss franc also firmed, USD/CHF down 0.41%. EUR/USD rose 0.12% to 1.122 and GBP/USD rose 0.12% to 1.345. In EM, the Mexican peso and Chinese yuan both firmed against the dollar, USD/MXN down 0.48% and USD/CNY down 0.18%, while the Turkish lira was the weak spot, USD/TRY up 0.14% to a fresh high of 50.08.
note.commodities: Energy bucked the risk-off tape, WTI up 3.50% to $91.20 and Brent up 4.89% to $99.25, a move that sits apart from the equity and metals complex and points to a supply or geopolitical driver rather than a demand read-through. Gold rose 0.61% to $4,097.90, a classic haven bid, but silver fell 0.56% and copper dropped 2.97% to $6.213, the industrial metals complex pricing growth concern rather than following gold higher. Palladium rose 3.42% and platinum rose 1.17%. Aluminium fell 1.88%. In ags, cocoa fell 3.04% and wheat was flat.
note.volatility: The vol surface moved into acute stress pricing. VIX rose 69.66% to 28.18 and VIX 9-day spiked 115.01% to 32.66, putting the front end above the 3-month print of 25.55, an inversion that signals the market is paying up heavily for near-term protection while longer-dated vol stays comparatively contained. VVIX rose 49.31% to 134.99, confirming the demand is concentrated in options on volatility itself, not just the underlying. SKEW eased slightly, down 1.01% to 149.37, so tail-risk pricing did not get materially more extreme even as at-the-money vol surged.
note.digital: Digital assets sold off in line with the equity unwind and then some. Bitcoin fell 6.01% to $75,573, Ether fell 8.13%, Solana fell 6.29% and XRP fell 6.83%. The move tracks the risk barometer's own reading, with bitcoin contributing -2.91 to the composite score, confirming crypto continues to trade as a high-beta risk asset rather than a hedge when equity vol spikes.
note.international: European closes were orderly by comparison, the EURO STOXX 50 down 0.55% and the DAX down 0.43%, with the CAC and IBEX both higher. Asia showed the dispersion that later hit Wall Street: the Nikkei fell 1.79% and the KOSPI dropped 5.28% on heavy tech exposure, while the Hang Seng rose 3.67% and the ASX 200 rose 2.61%. New York inherited a mixed setup, a soft but not broken Europe and an Asia session that already showed tech-specific pain in Korea, and then amplified it into the worst breadth reading of the period.
note.correlation:
The session reasserted the standard risk-off correlation stack. Equities fell, Treasuries rallied, the yen and franc firmed, and gold caught a bid, every piece behaving exactly as a flight-to-quality playbook would predict. The risk barometer's component contributions tell the same story: SPX, Russell and VIX each contributed -3.00, bitcoin -2.91, copper -2.31, all moving in the same direction at the same time.

The one crack worth watching is energy. Crude rose sharply while almost every other risk asset fell, a divergence that does not fit the standard correlation template. If oil keeps rising into a risk-off equity tape, that combination, weaker growth assets and firmer energy prices, tightens financial conditions from two directions at once. A continuation of that split, rather than oil rolling over with everything else, is the correlation break that would matter most for how this is read into next week.
